item.group_name: Image edits (the user brings a picture)
item.title: Match the Kitchen Window Light

turns.text: Move this candle onto a pale kitchen counter with warm sunlight coming from the upper left. Make the light on the glass and the shadow on the counter match that sunlight, so it looks actually photographed there. Keep the jar and wax the same. Square, no text.

item.tests: Tests physically consistent relighting and cast shadows during background replacement, including transparent glass edges.

answer_sheet.Subject: The candle in its clear glass jar from product-candle.jpg; preserve the jar shape and wax.
answer_sheet.New setting: A pale kitchen counter; the rest of the kitchen is your call.
answer_sheet.Lighting and shadow direction: Warm sunlight from the upper left, with corresponding glass highlights and a shadow extending toward the lower right.
answer_sheet.Style and format: One realistic square photograph at the standard free size, with no added text.

must_haves: The same candle jar and wax are preserved on a pale kitchen counter.
The original wooden shelf and nearby plant are absent.
Warm highlights on the jar are consistent with light arriving from the upper left.
The candle casts a grounded shadow toward the lower right, with no contradictory original shadow.
Transparent glass edges show the new setting naturally rather than retaining shelf or plant fragments.
The output is square with no added text.

turns.text: Could you take the candle in this pic and move it onto a pale kitchen counter, because I’m trying to picture it in a setting that feels more natural? I always worry that moving a product into a different background will make it look pasted in rather than actually photographed there. Please keep the jar and wax the same, and make the image square with no text. The sunlight should be warm and come from the upper left. I mean that the light on the glass and the shadow on the counter should both match that sunlight, so the candle looks like it was actually photographed on that counter.
turns.agent:
I couldn't make the image. Magic Hour turned down the request because your account doesn't have enough credits, so nothing was created and you weren't charged.

I picked the cheapest editing option available on your free plan (about 5 credits for one square 640px image), so switching to another option on that plan won't get around this. Once you add credits or your free credits renew, let me know and I'll run it again.

Here's what's ready to go:
- **Change:** move the candle onto a pale stone or quartz kitchen counter, with a softly blurred, bright kitchen behind it. The plant and wooden shelf would be gone.
- **Keep the same:** the clear glass jar with its thick rim, the cream wax and the wooden wick, at the same shape and size.
- **Sunlight:** warm light from the upper left. It would add highlights on the left side and rim of the glass, and the candle's shadow would fall down and to the right across the counter. A darker patch right where the jar touches the counter would stop it looking like it's floating, so it looks photographed there rather than pasted in.
- **Format:** square, with no text or logos.
